sections.html: Apionichthys nattereri is a purely freshwater flatfish of the family Achiridae (American sole). It grows to about 25 cm in length, making it one of the largest members of the genus.
The species is found throughout the Amazon basin. The imported animals came from Peru.

Like all flatfishes, these animals spend a large part of the day buried in fine sand, so their pretty spotted pattern is rarely seen in a properly set up aquarium. The tiny eyes sit on stalks and the mouth is also tiny.

There is no information about the reproduction. The animals are certainly egg-layers without brood care, but how, where and when the fish spawn and the larvae develop is unknown. Examination of the ear stones (otoliths) of two related freshwater species, A. finis and Hypoclinemus mentalis, revealed that these two species probably spawn in freshwater and never live in the sea, even as larvae (Matsushita et al., 2020).

The animals were first sent as Apionichthys finis, a closely related species that also occurs only in freshwater and is reported for Peru. Ramos's 2003 revision showed they were A. nattereri. In A. nattereri the dorsal, caudal and anal fins are clearly distinguishable from each other but nevertheless connected, whereas in A. finis the three fins are separated. The black border on the blind side is characteristic for A. nattereri and does not occur in any other species.

Among the Achiridae in South America, 26 species are known from freshwater, but many of them are euryhaline, living in the sea, brackish water and freshwater. A. nattereri lives exclusively in freshwater.
